rationale:
Evidence: iterations 0 and 1 (score 26.04 and 37.04) both left the line in all 60 trials. On the s-bend, progress was 0.040 and max_error was about 0.061 to 0.062 in every design, whatever the speed (1.3 to 1.7), kp (2 or 3), or kd (0.1 or 0.15). line_loss_events was exactly 1.0 in every trial. A failure point that does not move with speed or gain is more likely a sensing limit than a tuning problem. With five sensors at x = plus or minus 0.04 and a 0.012 footprint, the outermost sensor reaches about 0.046 m from the centre line. A tape edge at that point is about 0.058 m from the centre, which matches the observed max_error and loss point. Once the tape is outside the array, the robot is in line loss and drifts out.

What I accept from the round-2 critique: the revision confounded several changes (sensor y, footprint, mass, ki, base_speed, kd), and its geometry description was wrong. I also accept that the failure point is fixed, so speed and gain changes are unlikely to fix it. What I reject: I do not keep the revision's speed of 1.0, because it cannot finish and it gives no path toward a score. I do not keep kd 0.3, since its turn term is not shown to be safe.

What I changed, against the best raced design (iteration 1): sensor x spacing is widened from 0.02 to 0.03 m, spanning plus or minus 0.06 m. This extends the array's reach to about 0.072 m from the centre line, so the line should stay visible on the s-bend entry. Everything else is held at iteration 1 values (footprint 0.012, y 0.05, mass 0.8, base_speed 1.3, kp 3.0, kd 0.15, ki 0.02, last_direction, the same weights). A single-variable change keeps the result attributable. The gap between sensors (0.018 m) is still smaller than the 0.025 m tape, so at least one sensor always sees the line.

Expected result: s-bend progress rises clearly above 0.04 (about 60 percent confidence), and line_loss_events stays low. If progress is still 0.04, the cause is not the array reach, and the next test should be the line-loss rule (search_left or search_right). If the robot stays on track to the end of the course, the next step is to raise base_speed in steps of 0.1 while watching max_error (below 0.06 m).
